R501.note: Switches to Runtime.exec(String[]) closing shell-metachar injection on both OS branches; the disclosed dash-guard is narrow flag-injection hardening, not a behavior-breaking change.

R502.note: Standard mysql2 parameterized query (?, [trackingCode]) closes the injection with no other observable change.

R503.note: Generic error body replaces message/stack while logging is preserved; matches the app's own error-handler pattern.

R504.note: Strict allowlist on $plugin closes arbitrary-file inclusion; write-up openly flags that the allowlist values must be verified against the real plugins directory.

R505.note: crypto.randomBytes()/randomUUID() is the correct CSPRNG replacement for Math.random(); only the token format changes, as expected for this fix.

R506.note: Both options leave the flagged render_template_string(page_html) call rendering an attacker-influenced string as Jinja *source*; markupsafe.escape() (and the escaped {{term}} output in option 2) doesn't neutralize { }, so a `{{...}}` payload still survives into that second render as live Jinja/SSTI even though literal <script> tags are blocked.
